jobs.description:
**Company Overview**
====================

Each year, 2.5 trillion hours are spent on household chores. At Matic, we’re on a mission to recapture that lost time, and we’re doing it by revolutionizing home robotics.

Our first product, also called Matic, is a Wall-E-esque floor cleaning robot. We've built what amounts to "full self-driving in the home” with real-time 3D mapping, adaptive path-tracking, and a precise semantic understanding of the home. Our breakthroughs in spatial AI allow Matic to work reliably in real homes, using only RGB cameras and neural networks running on-device.

**Privacy First**
-----------------

What happens in the home, stays in the home. Our robots are private by design, with all data processing performed by the robot itself, not in the cloud.

**Our Approach**
----------------

Before the iPhone, consumers adopted several distinct devices; cell phones, PDAs, and portable music players each served a particular need. We believe in a similar progression for home robotics, starting with single-purpose robots and building iteratively toward more complex capabilities over time.

**Our Culture**
---------------

Matic is a tight-knit and collaborative team, singularly focused on building products our customers will cherish. We're ultra-hardworking people committed to solving tough problems that save precious time and energy.

**About the role**
==================

We're looking for a motivated perception engineer to join us on the ground floor, with a runway for huge and immediate impact.

**What you'll do**

* Translate open-ended, real-world problems into well-defined machine learning problems
* Design, build, and code computer vision-based algorithms

* Build novel neural network architectures
* Design and implement robust 3D geometry-based vision algorithms
* Build scalable machine learning infrastructure to train on large datasets and simultaneously be reproducible
* Analyze results, continuously update and improve accuracy & speed of various algorithms
* Deploy algorithms & machine learning pipelines at scale on the edge devices with limited compute without sacrificing performance
* Work to enable Level 5 autonomy in consumer robotics
* Cross-collaborate with Hardware, Electrical, and Systems teams to bring product vision to life

**What we look for**

* Robust machine learning background in computer vision and perceptual tasks, including 3D perception, multi-class object detection, 3D maps, and advanced robotics controls
* Track record of product-focused research applied to real-world applications
* Fluency with Rust (or C++) and Python (PyTorch or similar tools)
* Ability to write clean, reliable code that is easily maintained

**We'd love to hear from you if...**

* You are genuinely motivated to help those around you
* You are passionate about learning outside of your normal comfort zones
* You love diagnosing complex technical issues
* You are excited to do great work

**Compensation**

Base $140,000 — $220,000

Actual Compensation will depend on skills, experience and qualifications. Base Salary is one part of the total compensation package. The role is also eligible for equity through the company’s discretionary equity program, along with a comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental and vision coverage access to a 401(k) plan.

**About Anthropic**
-------------------

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

**About the role**
------------------

We're looking for engineers to join Model-to-Product Behavior Engineering, the team responsible for getting Claude's behavior right across Anthropic's products. You'll work with product, research, and safeguards teams to make sure Claude behaves in ways that are consistent, safe, and genuinely helpful, whether in a new feature, a new model, or a launch.

Evals are one of the sharpest tools we have for getting Claude's behavior right, but not the only one. You'll build evals to see clearly where Claude shines and where it slips, use what you learn to inform how to close the gap, and build the harness improvements that get us there. That takes your own intuition and judgment about model behavior, both to decide what is worth building and to know what to do with what you find. Your work will shape launch decisions and give research and product teams a signal they can trust.

You'll also build the infrastructure behind our evals, along with tooling that makes it easy to test and ship prompt fixes. And you'll create self-serve tools that let other teams build their own evals and improve Claude's behavior in their products, so that getting model behavior right scales well beyond any one team.

You'll work across many projects and product surfaces at once, holding a high bar for the details while adapting as model capabilities change.

Reactor is building the inference platform for real-time world models. Our goal is to democratize access to real-time intelligence to unlock next-generation use cases in media, physical AI and omni-directional models. We already run the largest and fastest catalog of world models on the market, and work closely with all major model labs to run and optimize their world models, including Alibaba, Amazon, and NVIDIA. Our team is made of alumni from leading firms such as Apple, Meta, Amazon, Microsoft, Luma AI, Adobe, Stability AI, and more. We've raised $74M led by Lightspeed, with Amplify Partners, WNDR, NVIDIA, Sapphire, and other Tier 1 investors participating. Jeffrey Katzenberg, co-founder of DreamWorks Animation, sits on our board of directors.

**The Role**

Robotics teams want to run the newest models on their robots. You'll build the product that makes that work.

You'll spend real time with our robotics customers, watch how they work, and turn what you see into software: a fix today, a feature next week, a platform capability when the same problem keeps showing up. One day that's debugging a robot-to-cloud connection. The next it's tightening a policy deployment workflow, or building a simulation view in the browser so a customer can see what their robot is about to do.

We want someone who can follow a problem all the way through the stack, and who cares as much about what the user sees as about how it's built.

This role is in person at our SF office.

**What You'll Do**
------------------

* Work directly with customers. Sit with their workflows, dig into failures, and figure out what would make their week easier.
* Turn open-ended asks into clear requirements, then decide what's a quick fix, what's a feature, and what belongs in the platform.
* Ship across the web UI, backend services, APIs and infrastructure.
* Trace problems across robot software, networking, cloud services and model inference, using logs, measurements and reproducible tests.
* Build simulation and visualization tools that let customers set up environments, inspect robot behavior and test policies.
* Keep up with robotics research and tooling, try what looks useful, and bring it into the product when it earns a place.

**Who You Are**
---------------

* You've shipped production software from first idea to people actually using it.
* Hands-on robotics experience. Deploying learned models or policies on physical robots is a big plus.
* You build across the stack, from front-end interfaces to backend services and infra.
* Product judgment: you talk to users, work out what they actually need, and decide what to build.
* You debug across application, networking and infrastructure boundaries without assuming the bug lives in one place.
* You read robotics research and can turn a good idea into working software.

**Bonus points**

* Python, C++, Rust, TypeScript/React or Go.
* ROS 2, MuJoCo or Isaac Sim.
* Interactive 3D, browser graphics or simulation interfaces.
* Policy serving, teleoperation, robotics datasets or evaluation workflows.
* Cloud infra, containers, WebRTC and real-time streaming.

You don't need all of these. We care most about what you've built, how you handle unfamiliar problems, and whether you can turn a customer's need into software.

**Benefits**
------------

* Competitive SF salary and meaningful early equity
* Visa sponsorship and relocation support
* Generous health, dental, and vision coverage

jobs.description:
**About Parameter**
-------------------

Security testing still mostly means scanners that miss the real bugs, or human pentesters who show up once a year. Parameter is building AI agents that do the work of a skilled attacker. They break into live applications, APIs and cloud environments, find the access control, auth and business logic flaws that matter, and prove each one before it's reported. We're a Y Combinator company in San Francisco.

The team is small and the engineers own large parts of the product. Some of the problems in front of us right now are below.

**Problems you might own**
--------------------------

* Keeping an agent on task and correct through a multi-hour engagement against a system it has never seen, and measuring whether a change made it better or worse
* Cutting false positives to near zero by building validation that proves a vulnerability is real before it is reported
* Running many long agent runs in parallel against customer infrastructure with strict isolation between customers, and making failures loud and cheap
* Turning what a skilled attacker does by hand into reliable agent capability
* Building the product customers use to review, verify and act on findings

**What the work looks like**
----------------------------

The role is broad on purpose. You will usually have a primary area (product, infrastructure, AI and agents, or offensive security) and you will work outside it whenever the company needs it. Day to day that means TypeScript, React and Next.js, GCP, Terraform, Temporal, LangGraph, Docker, Linear and Graphite. You work directly with the founders, talk to customers when it helps, and ship to production within days.

-------------------------

* You have built something real that people used, and can say exactly which parts were yours
* You have started something, whether a company, an open-source project, a product, or a research effort, and kept going when it was hard
* You have gone deep on something difficult without being asked: CTFs, bug bounty, CVEs, systems work, or competitive programming
* You learn quickly and are strong across more than one layer of the stack
* You decide things yourself, tell us what you decided and why, and see your work through after it ships
* Experience as a founder or founding engineer is a strong signal. Years at a large company and a long title are not what we are looking for

**How we work**
---------------

* In person in San Francisco, with long hours that we expect to continue at this stage. Most of the team works well beyond a normal week. If you want a balanced 9 to 5, this is not the right job
* A small team with high expectations and little process. You will have real scope, direct access to the founders, and fast decisions

Intro call with a founder (30 min), technical deep dive on something you built (60 min), a paid work trial of about one day, onsite with the team, then references and an offer. We aim to make an offer within two weeks of first contact.

$200K to $300K base salary depending on experience, plus 0.2% to 0.4% equity.

Full time, onsite in San Francisco. You must be authorized to work in the US. We are not able to sponsor visas at this time.

------------------------

Link to something you built or started and tell us which part was yours, and what broke. Please write this yourself. We read every answer.

Compensation Range: $200K - $300K

As a Forward Deployed Engineer on our Applied AI Inference team, you'll be the hands-on technical owner for a broad set of fast-growing customers building products on high-quality open models at scale. SPACE is Perplexity's sandbox platform. It's the isolated execution layer behind Perplexity Computer, the public Sandbox API, and a growing set of agent products. We built our own sandbox platform that lets us build the exact platform our products need: real pause and resume, forking, rolling snapshots, credential isolation, fine-grained network policy, and enterprise-grade encryption. * Drive performance and efficiency across the stack, from startup latency and resource density to cost.

**ABOUT MINERVA**
-----------------

Minerva builds AI for marketing leaders. We work together with marketers to automate and accelerate their workflows with AI agents. Our agents augment the end-to-end workflow of the marketer by automating analysis, campaign planning, activation, measurement and reporting.

Customers like the NBA, Ramp, Wander, Hard Rock Stadium Group and Luxury Presence use Minerva to develop a better understanding of their customers and introduce AI specifically built to understand the customer into their commercial organizations. Our campaigns outperform other tools because we built the entire stack: from identity to enrichment to data integration as well as agents to action and report on the analysis.

We've raised $20M from The General Partnership, 8VC, Lingotto, NBA Investments, Topology Ventures, Future Positive, Background Capital and many others. Our team brings together operators and investors from Citadel, Dentsu, Bridgewater, Meta Superintelligence, Growthloop, Amazon and Lazard, alongside engineers and researchers from Berkeley, MIT, Stanford and Cambridge.

**THE ROLE**
------------

A green job can still hide a stale input or a failed publication. By the time someone downstream notices, a customer usually has too.

You own pipeline health and actionable alerting across our first-party and third-party data. You cover our dbt pipelines and Dagster workflows, catch failures as they happen, and warn us about problems before they reach downstream delivery.

This is a mid-level individual contributor seat on the data platform team, reporting to our Head of Data Platform.

**WHAT YOU'LL DO**
------------------

* **Define what healthy means.** Freshness, completeness and successful-delivery expectations for our critical dbt and Dagster workflows and their Airflow and SQLMesh dependencies.
* **Build one alerting framework.** Clear severity, ownership, routing, deduplication and escalation, tuned so people trust it and don't mute it.
* **Catch problems early.** Detect missing deliveries, stalled runs and stale outputs. Add early warnings for growing lag, schema drift and abnormal volumes or coverage.
* **Trace the impact.** Connect health signals across dependencies to find the failing step and what it breaks downstream.
* **Keep recovery repeatable.** Maintain runbooks, and test detection and recovery on purpose.
* **Build checks into onboarding** so every new source arrives monitored. Agree data-quality thresholds with our data product team and measure detection time, recovery time and false positives.

**WHAT YOU HAVE**
-----------------

* Experience operating data transformation and orchestration systems, and diagnosing problems beyond job status. dbt and Dagster experience is valuable.
* You've built production monitoring and actionable alerts, including early warnings, and kept false positives down.
* You can tell a source delay from a processing failure from a quality regression, trace the impact and coordinate the fix with the pipeline's owner.
* You've maintained reusable checks and runbooks that other people used.
* You're in New York City or willing to relocate.

**NICE TO HAVES**
-----------------

* Data-quality frameworks.
* Anomaly detection.
* Service-level objectives for data.

**WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE**
---------------------------

* **First 90 days:** monitoring and alerting run on selected first- and third-party workflows, you've shown failure detection and early warnings in controlled tests, and the framework is part of onboarding.
* **The numbers you own:** detection time, recovery time and false-positive rate.

**COMPENSATION**
----------------

$170,000–$236,000 base salary, depending on level. Meaningful equity. Medical, dental and vision.

**HOW TO APPLY**
----------------

Skip the cover letter. Tell us about an alert you built that caught a real problem before anyone downstream noticed, and one you had to kill because it was noise.

**WHERE WE WORK**
-----------------

We work in person from our office at 300 Kent Avenue in Williamsburg, Brooklyn.

**BENEFITS**
------------

Every full-time role includes equity; medical, dental and vision coverage; unlimited PTO; a monthly fitness stipend; and an annual company offsite. We'd rather pay people well than buy perks nobody uses.

The salary range in this posting is our good-faith range for the role in New York City at the time of posting. Where an offer lands depends on the level and experience we see in the interview process.

**APPLYING**
------------

Apply on this page. We don't take applications by email, and we don't accept unsolicited submissions from recruiting agencies. If you need an accommodation at any point in the process, write to hiring@minerva.io.

**WORK AUTHORIZATION**
----------------------

You'll need to be authorized to work in the United States. We consider visa sponsorship case by case, so tell us on the application if you'll need it.

---------------------

Minerva is an equal opportunity employer. We make hiring decisions without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, citizenship status, age, disability, marital status, veteran status or any other characteristic protected by federal, New York State or New York City law.

Our hiring runs through Ashby and @minerva.io email addresses. We will never ask you for money, bank details or other financial information during the process. If a message claiming to be from Minerva looks wrong, forward it to hiring@minerva.io.
